Please read before applying

  • No government application fee. The official application to Saudi Arabian government universities is free of charge. Visa fees apply only after you are accepted. What we charge is a separate service fee for our assistance, not a government or university fee. If anyone asks you to pay for the application itself, an admission decision, or a "guaranteed" seat, it is not us and it is not the government — it is fraud. Do not pay anyone for this.
  • No one can guarantee a seat. Admission decisions are made only by the university and the Ministry of Education, after your application is reviewed. No one — including Arabex International or any other consultancy or agent — can guarantee you a seat or promise acceptance in advance. We can only advise and assist you with your application.
  • Replies take time. We are currently receiving applications and messages from a large number of students. Please be patient, and check this page and your WhatsApp regularly for updates and clarifications rather than sending repeat messages.

Part 1· 14 min read

Find your route

Start with who you are, then explore the opportunities open to you.

In short

  • Your residency status, not your nationality, decides where you apply.
  • Applying on the portal is free; each program is fully funded, partially funded or paid.
  • Iqama holders are usually asked for Qudurat and Tahsili; applicants from abroad usually aren't.
  • KFUPM and KAUST take applications on their own portals, not Study in Saudi.

Saudi universities do not share one set of rules — each sets its own requirements, test scores and weightings, and these can differ by major. Check the target university's own admission page before acting on any line. Labels: Official stated by the portal, a university, a ministry or an official guide. Field reported by applicants or students — useful, but not policy.

→

Start here

Who you are decides the route

Your residency status, not your nationality, decides where you apply and what you need.

ApplicantWhere to applyUsual testsTypical funding
International, living outside Saudi ArabiaStudy in Saudi portalNone by default; some programs ask for English or Arabic proofFull, partial or paid — set per program
International, living inside Saudi Arabia (iqama holder)Study in Saudi portal or the university's own admission site, depending on the universityQiyas: Qudurat (GAT), and often Tahsili (SAAT)Mostly paid at bachelor's level Field
Saudi nationalQabul portal (Ministry of Education)Qudurat and TahsiliNot covered here

Some programs are limited to Saudi nationals or iqama holders. Applicants from abroad are not eligible for those, so check the eligibility line on the program card before preparing a file.

1

Main route

Study in Saudi scholarships for international applicants

One free application on the Study in Saudi portal, with funding set program by program.

Open▾

Who can apply

  • Bachelor's and diploma: completed secondary school (12th / Plus Two or equivalent). Men and women.
  • Master's: a bachelor's degree. PhD: a master's degree.
  • Age limits are set by each university — check the program's own conditions before entering your date of birth.
  • Grades: applicants with roughly 75–80% or more are reported to have better chances. There is no single published cut-off. Field

Funding types Official

Every program card on the portal shows its funding type and yearly fee.

TypeWhat it covers
Full scholarshipEverything the university specifies — typically a monthly stipend, tuition exemption, university housing, travel ticket and health insurance
Partial scholarshipVaries by university: tuition only, or all benefits except health insurance, or all benefits except housing
Paid studyThe student pays tuition and all living costs

Work out the real monthly cost before you accept

Some partial scholarships do not include housing (Qassim and Umm Al-Qura were reported). With an 800 SAR stipend and 500 SAR rent, about 300 SAR is left for food, transport and everything else. Paid programs can also be very expensive — one card listed Artificial Intelligence (Bachelor's) at Prince Mugrin bin Abdulaziz University at 312,400 SAR a year.

Application windows

  • The portal opens in windows — recently two or three a year, sometimes only one. Each window lasts a few weeks. Official
  • Exact dates are set by the Ministry and announced shortly before each window — see the current cycle update at the top of this guide.
  • Universities and programs are added gradually during a window, not all at once — check back if a university shows no programs yet. Field
  • Some universities interview applicants first. Umm Al-Qura's interviews have run about 4–5 minutes, on Arabic background and use. Field

Arabic language diplomas

Arabic institutes for non-native speakers are units of the universities, not separate institutions. You apply for the diploma as one of that university's programs, on the same portal and in the same window as a bachelor's.

UniversityInstituteWhat its own pages and reports say
Islamic University of Madinahمعهد تعليم اللغة العربية لغير الناطقين بهاFor international scholarship applicants it is the first stage of the scholarship; recent cohorts began it remotely
Umm Al-Qura University, MakkahInstitute of Arabic Language for Non-Native SpeakersUniversity page: 2-year scholarship with books, housing, medical care, annual ticket and 850 SAR a month; prepares students to join UQU colleges. Check current terms
Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, Riyadh (women)Arabic Language Institute for Non-Arabic SpeakersDiploma of 4 levels, 60 credit hours; scholarship age 17–25. PNU states there is currently no bridging to its bachelor's
Imam Muhammad bin Saud Islamic University, Riyadhمعهد تعليم اللغة العربيةArabic-teaching diploma has been offered as a partial scholarship Field
King Saud University, RiyadhArabic Linguistics Institute (معهد اللغويات العربية)University page: intensive program for scholarship students
  • Funding is set per program on its portal card — not every diploma is fully funded.
  • Finishing a diploma does not by itself secure a bachelor's place. Some universities let strong graduates move on to their colleges; PNU requires a new application.

Hamza test — proof of Arabic level Official

The official Arabic proficiency test of the King Salman Global Academy for Arabic Language (KSAA), recognised on the Study in Saudi portal. It is different from a diploma: it only proves your level.

ItemDetail
SkillsListening 35 min, Reading 60 min, Writing 40 min, Speaking 20 min (155 min total)
LevelsA2 to C1, based on CEFR
FormatComputer-based; in person at centres in Saudi Arabia, or remote worldwide
Registrationforms.ksaa.gov.sa/ar/hamza
Age16 or older on the test date
ContactHamza@ksaa.gov.sa
  • Your name must match your passport exactly — no edits are allowed after registration.
  • Remote tests are cancelled for switching tabs, a second person on camera, your face not being visible, copy-paste or stopping screen share.
  • Applicants who submitted before their certificate arrived found it attached automatically by passport number. Field
2

Residents

Iqama holders already living in Saudi Arabia

Residents apply under different rules: many universities ask for Qiyas test scores, and most bachelor's places for this group are paid.

Open▾

Where to apply

  • Some universities take iqama holders through the Study in Saudi portal; others through their own admission site. The university's Admission and Registration page says which.
  • Vacancies window (شواغر): a window for remaining seats usually opens after the initial-acceptance phase ends. Follow the portal and its official X account, @StudyInSaudiAr. Field

Qiyas admission tests

Run by ETEC and registered through ETEC's Qiyas e-services at etec.gov.sa.

TestMeasuresWho needs itFee (approx.)Retakes and validity
Qudurat / GAT (قدرات)Verbal and quantitative reasoning — aptitude, not curriculumAlmost all applicants in this group, all tracks100 SAR early paper; 150 SAR late paper or digital; 200 SAR outside the KingdomUp to 5 attempts in total; results valid about 5 years
Tahsili / SAAT (تحصيلي)High-school physics, chemistry, biology and mathsScience and health tracks (medicine, engineering, pharmacy, dentistry) and often Shariah tracks; not most humanitiesAbout 100 SAR (computer, paid via SADAD)Separate windows, fewer retakes than Qudurat
  • Qudurat has two versions: a science-track test and a theoretical-track test (Shariah and business). The fee shown in your ETEC account is the one that counts.
  • “Tahsili wal Qudurat” means both tests together — it is not a separate exam, and not the American SAT.
  • Avoid qiyas.sa, which is reported to be a commercial prep site, not the official channel.

How selection is scored

  • Admission is usually a weighted formula of school grades, Qudurat and Tahsili. Weights vary by university and major.
  • Example — KFUPM Vacancies Track: Qudurat 50% + Tahsili 40% + school 10%. Official

Costs and support

At bachelor's level most programs for iqama holders are paid, from about 2,000 SAR a semester upward, and universities generally do not give this group housing or a stipend. Field

If you are inside Saudi Arabia when the visa stage comes, you must exit first — see Step 7: The educational visa.

3

Madinah

Islamic University of Madinah — three separate tracks

Applicants often confuse these tracks, so keep them apart.

Open▾
TrackFormatCost to studentWhere to apply
International scholarship (in person)Starts with a remote Arabic stage, then study in MadinahScholarship; no stipend during the remote stageStudy in Saudi portal, then the university's Minhatee system
Bachelor of Shariah (distance learning)Fully online, in Arabic, one fixed study plan230 SAR application + 230 SAR placement test if required; study fees covered by the Waqf scholarshipdistancelearning.iu.edu.sa
Micro-Credential e-coursesOnline, one or several courses; can build toward a diploma or bachelor'sPaid per courseDistance-learning portal, in announced windows

A. International scholarship (in person)

  1. Apply through the Study in Saudi portal when the university's programs are open.
  2. Complete the second step on Minhatee when the email arrives. Minhatee has its own document list.
  3. The status may read: “You have been accepted to the Arabic Language Teaching Institute remotely.”
  4. Study Arabic remotely, up to one academic year. No monthly stipend is paid during this stage.
  5. In previous cohorts, students received final acceptance after one or two semesters and the required tests, then travelled to Madinah. Some who finished a full remote year were still waiting because of delays.

Hafiz applicants are reported to receive priority in Islamic faculties. Field

B. Bachelor of Shariah (distance learning) Official

Offered with the King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Waqf for His Parents.

  • Who can apply: non-Saudi men and women living outside the Kingdom, with a recognised secondary certificate, never dismissed from any institution, fully fluent in Arabic (others must pass a placement test) and medically fit for distance study.
  • Documents: secondary certificate, transcript, police clearance and valid passport — scanned from originals; a photo of a photo is rejected.
  • Steps: apply on the official distance-learning portal, create a student account, pay the non-refundable registration fee, sit the Arabic placement test if required, and receive a university number on acceptance.
ItemAmountPaid by
Application and file activation230 SARApplicant, non-refundable
Arabic placement test (if required)230 SARApplicant, non-refundable even if failed
Semester fees after the first230 SAR eachWaqf scholarship
Credit units230 SAR per unitWaqf scholarship
Repeat exam115 SAR eachWaqf scholarship
Graduation and certificate575 SARWaqf scholarship
  • The scholarship continues only while you meet the Waqf's conditions and stay in good standing.
  • To earn the degree you must pass the full plan, reach the required GPA and pass an in-person comprehensive final exam at a university venue, at your own expense.
  • A computer with camera and microphone is mandatory — phones and tablets are not accepted for exams.

The university's own warnings

Apply only through the official portal. The university has no offices or agents anywhere. Apply personally and keep your numbers safe. Submission does not mean acceptance, and forgery cancels admission.

C. Micro-Credential e-courses

  • Register for one course or several, and build toward a diploma or bachelor's according to the study plan.
  • Windows are announced on the distance-learning portal. After acceptance, log in and approve the declaration (الإقرار) to finalise admission.
  • Check acceptance only in your own portal account.
4

Science & research

KFUPM and KAUST

English-taught science, engineering and research universities with their own application portals.

Open▾

Both universities take applications on their own portals, not the Study in Saudi portal, and teach in English.

KFUPM, Dhahran — bachelor's tracks Official

TrackWhoHow selectedUsual timing
SAT TrackInternational applicants and residents in KSASAT 1350+ in one sitting, then an online KFUPM maths testEarly February
Primary TrackMainly applicants inside KSA50% Qudurat + 50% KFUPM Tahsili test (via Qiyas)January
Olympiad TrackSaudis and children of Saudi mothers onlyInternational Science Olympiad winnersMay – July
Vacancies TrackRemaining seatsQudurat 50% + Tahsili 40% + school 10%After the main tracks

SAT Track steps (applicants from abroad)

  1. Take the SAT and score 1350 or more in a single sitting (no superscoring).
  2. Send scores through College Board directly to KFUPM.
  3. Register on apply.kfupm.edu.sa during the SAT Track window (early February in recent years), with a recommendation letter and statement of purpose.
  4. Sit the online maths test when KFUPM emails the date.
  5. Attend an interview if requested, and confirm your major within 24 hours of the offer. KFUPM arranges the visa after admission.
  • Eligibility: school finished within the last three years; science stream or an international school in natural sciences; never studied at KFUPM. School marks, Qudurat, Tahsili and IELTS/TOEFL are not used for this track.
  • 1350 is only the minimum to apply — about 1550+ is reported as realistic for international applicants. Field
  • The undergraduate scholarship includes a full tuition waiver, a 1,000 SAR monthly stipend, free textbooks and subsidised meals. Official
  • Applicants outside Saudi Arabia should confirm their route with admissions@kfupm.edu.sa before preparing.

KFUPM graduate (MS, PhD)

  • Scholarships for all PhD and selected MS programs: tuition waiver, monthly stipend, furnished housing, annual air tickets, medical care and subsidised meals.
  • English: TOEFL 70 / IELTS 6.0 / Duolingo 105 for MS; 80 / 6.5 / 120 for PhD. GPA 3.0 out of 4.
  • Fall-intake applications usually open around May–June on cgis.kfupm.edu.sa. Contact: gs-admissions@kfupm.edu.sa.

KAUST, Thuwal — graduate only

ItemDetail
ProgramsMS and PhD in 17 STEM programs. No bachelor's.
EntryRelevant bachelor's for MS, relevant master's for PhD; age 18+; GPA 3.0 minimum
EnglishIELTS 7 (6.5 each), TOEFL iBT, PTE 71 or Cambridge 185; Duolingo and MOI letters not accepted
DocumentsTranscripts, CV, a statement of purpose of about 750 words, 3 referees, passport
FellowshipTuition, monthly stipend, free housing, health insurance, visa and travel support
TimingApplications usually open in late September and close in early January; programs start in late August

Confirm KAUST details

Check every KAUST figure on admissions.kaust.edu.sa before applying. Applying is free; one application and one program per year.
5

Self-funded

Private universities and colleges

For students who can pay some or all costs.

Open▾

Private institutions suit students who can pay some or all costs and do not want to wait on scholarship cycles.

College of Law and Islamic Sciences, Madinah (new, private) Official

  • Bachelor of Sharia in an Arabic track or an English track; 4 years, 180 credit hours.
  • Men and women in separate buildings; in person only. In its first year, classes are held on the Islamic University of Madinah campus while the college's own campus is built.
  • Admission: secondary certificate or equivalent, GAT or equivalent (SAT accepted), Achievement Test if required, passport or iqama, two photos, application fee receipt, and attestation for certificates issued outside the Kingdom.
Fee basisStandardFirst international intake (30% off)Group of 2+ (40% off)
Total for 4 years100,600 SAR70,420 SAR60,360 SAR
  • The discount is fixed for all 4 years once approved. Housing, food and airfare are not included.
  • Refunds: 100% before the semester (except the application fee), 80% in week 1, 50% in week 2, 25% in week 3, none after.

Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University, Al-Qassim

A non-profit private university (fully NCAAA-accredited). Programs open to international applicants on the portal as partial scholarships:

ProgramLanguageYearsAnnual fee (SAR)After partial scholarship (SAR)
NursingEnglish469,00048,300
Midwifery (women)English469,00048,300
Medical LaboratoryEnglish557,50040,250
Finance and Risk ManagementArabic / English446,00032,209
ManagementArabic446,00032,200
Accounting and Information SystemsArabic446,00032,200

Medicine (MBBS)

Medicine is not listed on the portal for international applicants at Al-Rajhi. Check each program card carefully — nobody can promise a medicine seat.
6

Islamic study

The Two Holy Mosques and other structured Islamic study

Programs outside the university system, with their own registration channels.

Open▾

These programs sit outside the university system and have their own registration channels.

Institute and College of the Prophet's Mosque and the Grand Mosque

  • Run under the General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques (gph.gov.sa).
  • Ma'had (Institute): intermediate and secondary levels, for boys and girls, full-time or affiliated.
  • Kulliyah (College): 4-year bachelor's in Shariah, Quran, Sunnah, Aqeedah and Arabic, with sections for men and women. The Grand Mosque in Makkah has its own college and institute, with written and oral entrance tests.
  • Enrolment categories: Muntadhim (in person), Muntasib (online study with in-person exams) and Mustami' (listener, not formally enrolled).
  • Selection is based on Quran memorisation, an entrance exam and an interview.

Distance Quran and Mutoon circles, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi Official

  • Run by the mosque's Department of Quran and Scholarly Texts Circles, and open to international students, including from India.
  • Memorise the Quran and the mutoon in proper order, with the option of an ijāza (sanad) on completion, and a revision track for those who have already memorised.
  • Register at reg.qm.edu.sa. Some online classes marketed as “Masjid Nabawi classes” are run by outside academies — check the source.

Scientific Foundational Methodology Program, Buraidah

  • برنامج المنهجية العلمية التأصيلية, run by Markaz al-Nukhab al-Ilmiyyah, a waqf institution in Buraidah, Al-Qassim.
  • Four stages — Ta'sees, Ta'seel, Bina' and Tamkeen — each with set texts and assessments.
7

Women

Study options for women

Women can apply to most Saudi universities, which run separate women's campuses or sections — but fully funded options for women from abroad are fewer than for men.

Open▾
  • In recent windows, Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University (PNU, Riyadh) has been the main — at times the only — university on the portal offering fully funded scholarships to women, for bachelor's or the Arabic diploma. Field
  • Other universities with women's campuses or programs include Taibah University (Madinah), King Abdulaziz University (Jeddah), Umm Al-Qura University (Makkah), Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University (Midwifery is women-only) and the College of Law and Islamic Sciences, Madinah.
  • The Islamic University of Madinah's distance Bachelor of Shariah and the Prophet's Mosque distance circles are open to women.
  • Profile photo: the face must be visible. Women's applications are reviewed by women. Field

Mahram requirement — confirm before applying

A mahram (father, brother or husband) accompanying the student, or already resident in Saudi Arabia, has generally been required for women's study visas. Reports say this has recently changed, but it is not clear whether that applies to every university or only some programs. Confirm the current rule with the university and the visa instructions.
Part 2· 11 min read

Apply step by step

The eight stages from preparing documents to arriving in the Kingdom.

In short

  • Prepare every document before the window opens — the police clearance can take weeks.
  • Translate your documents into Arabic; many admission staff read only Arabic.
  • A new application cancels the old one, and confirming an acceptance cancels your other choices.
  • Leave Saudi Arabia before applying for the educational visa.

The whole journey

Eight stages. The waiting sits in the middle — stages five and six are where most of the time goes.

  1. {{ o.num }} {{ o.title }} {{ o.note }}
1

Step one

Before You Apply

Your route depends on where you are living now. Establish which one applies to you before anything else — the two paths diverge immediately.

Route A

Applying from outside Saudi Arabia

You apply through the official Study in Saudi portal at studyinsaudi.moe.gov.sa. This is the main route, and it covers most international applicants.

Route B

Already inside Saudi Arabia, holding an iqama

Sometimes you apply through the portal; sometimes through the university's own Admission & Registration site. It genuinely depends on the university, so check that university's own site rather than assuming.

Prepare your documents before the window opens

Application windows are open for a limited period, not all year. Gathering certificates, clearances and translations takes weeks — starting only when the window opens is what causes most missed cycles. Start gathering them now, whenever the next window opens. Both fully-funded scholarship places and self-funded study exist, so decide which you are pursuing early.

Every university sets its own rules

Saudi universities do not share one set of criteria. Check the Admission and Registration Department (إدارة القبول والتسجيل) page of each university, and confirm the program is open to international applicants — some are only for Saudi nationals or iqama holders. Tests you may be asked for:

  • Qudurat (GAT) and Tahsili (SAAT) — Saudi national tests taken through Qiyas/ETEC. These are mainly for iqama holders already living in Saudi Arabia, especially those who studied the Saudi curriculum. Applicants from abroad are usually not asked for them, though a few universities ask for them or an accepted alternative such as the SAT. Tahsili covers high-school science and maths — it is not the American SAT.
  • IELTS / TOEFL — for English-taught programs that ask for it. Book only through the official IELTS and ETS websites.
  • Arabic proficiency — some Arabic-taught programs have their own test or a preparatory Arabic year. The Hamza test from the King Salman Global Academy is the recognised proof of Arabic level.

Know the funding type before you choose

Each program card shows its funding: full scholarship (typically stipend, tuition, housing, ticket and insurance), partial scholarship (varies — sometimes without housing) or paid study (you pay everything). Work out the real monthly cost before you apply. Every route, program type and Arabic diploma is explained in Part 1: Find your route.
2

Step two

Prepare Your Documents

The mandatory documents are the ones without which you cannot submit. The supporting documents are not required, but they are what makes a file competitive.

Mandatory

Without these you cannot submit.

  • {{ d.t }}{{ d.d }}

Supporting

Not required, but they strengthen the file.

  • {{ d.t }}{{ d.d }}

Document quality decides more than people expect

Every scan should be clear and complete, with the whole document visible in frame, names and dates readable, and no shadows across the page. Follow the portal's own format and size rules. A poor photograph or an unreadable certificate can cause outright rejection — the most avoidable reason applications fail.

  • Your passport should be valid for a good period — at least 6 months is the common advice.
  • Your name must be spelled exactly the same on your passport, certificates and translations.
  • Scan in colour, straight, with all four corners visible. Phone photos with shadows are often rejected.
  • Name files clearly, e.g. Passport_Name.pdf or Transcript_BA_Name.pdf.
  • When there is only one upload slot, keep the original and its Arabic translation together in one PDF.
  • Scan from originals — a photo of a photo, or an incomplete file, is rejected.
  • Police clearance can take weeks (in India, through Passport Seva) — start it early.

Writing a Statement of Purpose, asking for recommendation letters or preparing a CV? See Strengthen your file below.

3

Step three

Translate Into Arabic

Your academic certificate, your transcript and your supporting documents commonly need an Arabic translation alongside the originals.

Strongly advised, even where it isn't currently enforced

The portal is new and may at present accept submissions without translations. Translation has been required in past years, and many admission staff work only in Arabic — a file they can read is a file they can assess. Verify the current requirement on the official portal before deciding to skip it.

Applying through the portal is free. Certified Arabic translation by Arabex is a paid service, and we tell you the cost before any work begins.

4

Step four

Register & Submit on the Portal

With your documents ready, the submission itself is straightforward.

  1. {{ s.n }} {{ s.v }}

How many universities and programs you may choose can change from one cycle to the next. Check the live portal for the current number rather than relying on what applied last year.

A new application cancels the previous one

If you already have an application for an academic program, submitting a new one automatically cancels it. Plan your university choices carefully before you submit.

Rules that catch people out

  • Enter your name exactly as in your passport. Application data cannot be changed after submission — only contact details.
  • The passport number can be changed only on a new account with no applications submitted.
  • Programs appear on the portal gradually during a window. If a university shows no programs yet, check back.
  • Read each program card before adding it: funding type, yearly fee, language, gender and duration — and whether it is open to applicants from abroad.
  • The portal's terms prohibit impersonation. Anyone helping you should guide you through your own submission, not operate your account.
5

Step five

University Review, then Initial Acceptance

The university examines your qualifications and your documents against its own criteria. Initial acceptance can take anywhere from a few weeks to many months. This is normal, and silence during it does not mean rejection.

Before you confirm an initial acceptance

Confirming an initial acceptance cancels all your other preferences. Check the program's funding type and fee first — confirming a paid program you cannot afford is one of the costliest mistakes. Some acceptance emails give a deadline to respond (for example 5 days).

Interviews and rejections

  • Some universities interview applicants during review — for example remote interviews by Northern Border University, and short interviews by Umm Al-Qura on Arabic background.
  • Rejection emails look the same whatever the reason. Don't read a cause into them; where reapplication is allowed, improve the file and apply in the next window.
  • Deferral is not automatic — get written confirmation from the university.

If you applied to Islamic University of Madinah

A second application is mandatory

After your initial registration, Madinah applicants receive an email asking them to complete a second application on the university's own Minhatee portal. Without that second step your file is not reviewed at all — so watch your inbox and your spam folder. Online Shariah studies at Madinah are handled through Minhatee only.

6

Step six

Ministry Processing, then Final Acceptance

Once the university approves you, your application moves to the Ministry of Education for final approval. Scholarship funds are allocated at this stage and an invitation letter is issued.

How long this takes varies widely. Some applicants hear back within weeks; others wait considerably longer. Keep checking your email and the portal, and keep your documents current in case anything is requested again.

Start attestation as soon as you are accepted

Attestation is usually not needed to apply, but it is often needed after acceptance or on arrival. Umm Al-Qura's acceptance notices, for example, have asked new students to bring their original secondary certificate and transcript attested by the Saudi embassy or cultural attaché, plus a certified medical report and good-conduct certificate.

Watch for an arrival deadline

Acceptance notices can set a mandatory arrival window — one Umm Al-Qura notice gave about a month, after which the admission and scholarship were cancelled without deferral. Check the dates on your own notice.
7

Step seven

The Educational Visa

Important

You must be outside the Kingdom to submit the visa application

Applicants physically inside Saudi Arabia must exit before submitting the electronic educational visa, or the application is automatically rejected. If you hold only initial acceptance, wait inside the Kingdom until final acceptance arrives, then depart, then apply.

  • {{ v.v }}
8

Step eight

Travel & Arrival

Collect your visa — from the embassy or as an e-visa — and travel. Two things follow arrival.

Medical checks

A medical exam is not currently required for the e-visa itself. If the visa stage asks for one, it is a Wafid medical booked before travel. After you arrive, follow your university's instructions for any checks needed to settle your status.

Housing

Many fully-funded scholarships include university accommodation. Check what your offer covers before you look for anything — renting is only necessary if housing is not provided.

If you do need to rent, a contract can be registered officially through Ejar, including on an educational visa. An official contract in your own name protects your rights as a tenant.

Educational-visa holders can register a contract on Ejar without an iqama, through an accredited Ejar agent. Before accepting a partial scholarship, budget rent, food, transport and phone together — they can absorb the whole stipend.

Rules for female applicants and mahram are changing

Verify the current official visa and university requirements directly rather than relying on the experience of applicants from previous years. What was true two cycles ago may not be true now.

On arrival

  • New students have been receiving a Visitor ID on entry instead of the old iqama; some linked services are still rolling out.
  • Keep your passport safe — a lost passport delays the residency steps.
Part 3· 8 min read

Strengthen your file

The documents that turn a complete application into a competitive one.

In short

  • Answer the exact question in your Statement of Purpose, within the word limit.
  • Ask referees who know you well, and give them a small file about you.
  • Keep every date on your CV matching your certificates.
  • Tick the final checklist before you press submit.

Your statement, your letters, your CV — and a final check before you submit. Open any section.

Plan and track your applicationsOne page of notes per university ▾

Successful applicants are usually well organised. Before you submit, make one page of notes for every university you choose, so you don't miss a document or a requirement. For each one, note:

  • University and program, and the degree level (Bachelor's, Master's, PhD)
  • Whether it is open to international applicants, and any age or grade requirement
  • Tests needed (Qudurat, Tahsili, IELTS, Arabic)
  • How many recommendation letters, and whether a Statement of Purpose or research proposal is needed
  • Whether a scholarship is available
  • Documents uploaded, and your status: initial acceptance, final acceptance or rejected

Three things admissions committees look for

  1. Fit. Why this program suits you matters more than marks alone.
  2. Specific but flexible. Name your area of interest clearly, and show you are open to learning.
  3. Ability and passion. Show you can do the work and that you truly care about the subject.

Good practice: prepare your full file for one university first, then adapt it for the others. Don't submit to your first choice until your documents are complete and checked.

Write your Statement of PurposeStructure, length, and mistakes to avoid ▾

A Statement of Purpose — also called a motivation letter or personal statement — tells the university who you are and why you want to study there. Mainly asked for postgraduate programs. Most questions come down to three things:

1 · Where are you coming from?Your education, background and what led you to this subject.
2 · Why this program?Why this subject, this university and Saudi Arabia.
3 · Where are you going after?Your goals, and how this degree helps you serve your community.

Step by step

  1. Read the question carefully and answer exactly that question — many essays fail because they don't.
  2. Collect your material first: the teachers, books, scholars and experiences that shaped your interest, your best projects or papers, and your skills.
  3. Write an honest first draft in simple language. Focus on content, not style.
  4. Edit for the reader. Turn casual phrases into clear academic language — "I had a part-time job in the library" becomes "I assisted in cataloguing the Arabic manuscripts collection at …".
  5. Add specifics: the exact department, program or areas of study that interest you at that university.
  6. Ask a teacher to review it, then proofread for spelling and grammar.

Length

If the university gives a limit, get close to it but never exceed it. If no limit is given, aim for roughly 500–1,000 words.

Suggested structure

1. Opening. A short, real moment or question that drew you to your subject, then the program you are applying for.

2. Your preparation. Studies, key courses, teachers, the books or scholars you studied with, your best project, and the skills you gained.

3. Experience. Teaching, da'wah, translation, research, volunteering or work — and what each taught you.

4. Why this university. The specific program or department, and why studying in Saudi Arabia matters for your goals.

5. Your future. What you plan to do after graduating and how you will benefit your community.

Closing. One or two sentences on your readiness and commitment.

Explaining weak marks or a gap

Keep the statement positive. Explain a low mark or gap year briefly and without drama — and only if the problem is in the past, has been resolved, is understandable and is unlikely to happen again. If your marks improved year by year, say so.

Avoid

  • Spelling and grammar errors
  • Opening with "Since childhood I have always wanted to…"
  • Not answering the actual question
  • Writing what you think they want to hear
  • Copying a sample or someone else's essay
  • Long excuses or personal problems
  • Going over the word limit
  • Defining your subject to experts ("Islamic studies is…")
  • Empty self-praise ("I am hardworking and intelligent")

Do

  • Describe one or two real experiences in detail
  • Show qualities through actions, not adjectives
  • Name the teachers, books or projects that influenced you
  • Refer to your other documents ("see attached CV")
  • Explain clearly why this university
  • State a realistic plan after graduation
  • Use your own words and be truthful
  • Keep the tone respectful and confident

Language: if the program is taught in Arabic, writing your statement in good Arabic — or attaching an Arabic version — shows your readiness. Make sure the Arabic is correct and checked.

Get strong recommendation lettersWho to ask, what to give them, what a good letter says ▾

Alongside your marks, tests and statement, recommendation letters are one of the main sources of information about you. For borderline applicants, one strong, detailed letter can make a real difference.

Who to ask

Choose people who know you well and can write in detail, who will speak positively about your ability and character, and who will submit on time. A detailed letter from a teacher or supervisor who knows your work is worth far more than a short one from a famous person who barely knows you. If you did a project or thesis, the university will expect a letter from your supervisor.

Islamic and Sharia programs: some universities ask for a recommendation (تزكية) from a recognised Islamic centre, institution or scholar, and may specify how many. Check the exact requirement on the university's website.

How to ask

  • Ask early — your referees are busy people.
  • Ask honestly: "What would you be able to say about me?" If they seem hesitant, ask someone else. A weak letter can do more harm than good.
  • Remind them politely, about once a week, until it is done.
  • Where allowed, get one extra letter beyond the minimum, in case one is delayed.

Give your referee a small file

  • Your mark sheets, or a list of your main subjects with grades
  • One of your best papers, assignments or projects
  • Your CV and a draft of your Statement of Purpose
  • The university and program, with any required format
  • A short note on what you would like them to highlight

What a strong letter contains

1. Introduction. Who the referee is, how long and in what role they have known you, and a clear recommendation for [program] at [university].

2. Knowledge and skills. What you have mastered — e.g. Arabic grammar, Fiqh, Hadith sciences, research methods, Qur'an memorisation.

3. A standout example. One or two concrete stories where you went above and beyond.

4. Character. Manners, discipline, reliability and religious commitment, with an example where possible.

5. Closing. A clear statement of confidence and a recommendation without reservation.

Signature block. Name, position, institution, phone/email, signature, seal and date.

Format: on the institution's official letterhead, with the referee's full name, position, contact details, signature, date and official seal or stamp — submitted with an Arabic translation.

Honesty: letters must be genuinely written and signed by the referee. Universities may contact referees to confirm a letter, and a false or self-written letter can lead to rejection.

Prepare your CVA simple academic CV in 1–2 pages ▾

Keep it to 1–2 pages, clear and truthful, with the most recent items first.

Header: full name (as in passport) · nationality · date of birth · email · phone

Education: degree, institution, years, grade — plus any Islamic or Hifz studies with the institution and year

Qur'an memorisation: amount memorised, ijazah if any, and from whom

Languages: Arabic, English and mother tongue, with level and any test scores

Teaching / work experience: role, organisation, dates and one or two lines on what you did

Research, writing and translation: projects, articles or translations, with titles

Awards and certificates: competitions, courses, prizes

Activities and service: da'wah, volunteering, community work

Referees: name, position, institution and contact for 2–3 referees

Tip: use a plain, professional layout and avoid long paragraphs. Every date on your CV should match your certificates.

Research proposal (postgraduate)For research master's and PhD applicants ▾

Research master's and PhD applicants may be asked for a short proposal, often 2–5 pages. Follow any template the university gives. A general structure:

  1. Title — specific and clear
  2. Background — the topic and why it matters
  3. Research problem and questions — narrow enough to answer
  4. Previous studies — what has been written, and the gap your study fills
  5. Methodology — sources, manuscripts, field work, analysis
  6. Expected contribution — what your research will add
  7. Timeline and references

Arabic-taught programs often use this structure:

خطة البحث: العنوان، المقدمة، مشكلة البحث، أسئلة البحث، أهداف البحث، الدراسات السابقة، منهج البحث، خطة الفصول، المصادر والمراجع.

Prepare for admission and language testsQudurat, Tahsili, IELTS/TOEFL, Arabic ▾
  • Don't go in without preparation — studying improves your score.
  • Use the official practice materials and take as many full practice tests as you can.
  • Revise the basics, especially maths for aptitude tests.
  • Book early so your result arrives before the application deadline.
  • Qudurat and Tahsili are mainly for iqama holders inside Saudi Arabia; Qudurat fees are roughly 100–150 SAR through the Qiyas/ETEC portal. Book IELTS and TOEFL only through their official websites.
Final checklist before you submitTick every line before you press submit ▾
  • I have confirmed the program is open to international applicants.
  • I have read each university's Admission and Registration page.
  • My name is spelled the same on my passport, certificates and translations.
  • All scans are clear, in colour and complete.
  • Arabic translations are attached with my academic and other documents.
  • My police clearance is ready, with its Arabic translation.
  • My Statement of Purpose answers the exact question and is within the word limit.
  • My recommendation letters are on letterhead, signed, stamped and dated.
  • My CV is up to date and its dates match my certificates.
  • My test results, if required, are uploaded.
  • I have chosen my universities carefully — a new application cancels the previous one.
  • I have saved copies of everything I submitted.
  • I will check My Applications regularly, including my email's spam folder.
Part 4· 2 min read

Stay safe

Scams, common mistakes and corrections to guides going around.

In short

  • Nobody can sell an admission, and the portal never charges to apply.
  • Check an acceptance only inside your own portal account.
  • Be careful with guides that mix old and new rules.
!

Stay safe

Scams, common mistakes and corrections

Most costly errors come from fake notices, confirming the wrong offer, or trusting guides that mix old and new rules.

Scams

  • Forged acceptance notices have circulated. Verify acceptance only inside your own portal account or the official university system.
  • Universities such as the Islamic University of Madinah state they have no offices or agents anywhere. Nobody can sell an admission.
  • The portal does not charge to apply. Genuine official payments are things like the MoFA visa fee or a registration fee for certain online programs.

Common mistakes

  • Confirming an initial acceptance for a paid program you cannot afford — it cancels all your other preferences.
  • Applying without checking whether a program is limited to Saudi nationals or iqama holders.
  • Applying for the visa from inside Saudi Arabia.
  • Typing your name differently from your passport — it cannot be edited after submission.
  • Leaving the police clearance until the window opens.

Corrections to guides going around

Claim you may have seenWhat we found
Main intake is March–May with 90%+ of seatsNot confirmed for the new portal; windows vary
Iqama holders: Qiyas tests are mandatoryRequired by many universities, not all — check each university
Qiyas website: qiyas.saOfficial registration is through ETEC (etec.gov.sa); qiyas.sa is reported to be a commercial prep site
The Arabic diploma is free with full scholarship and guarantees a bachelor'sFunding varies by university; PNU has no bridging to its bachelor's
Arabic diploma only at Madinah, Umm Al-Qura and PNUAlso at Imam Muhammad bin Saud and King Saud universities
KFUPM full scholarship needs SAT 1500+The official minimum to apply is 1350; about 1550+ is reported as realistic
Visa needs a GAMCA medical and stamping via an agencyThe current route is the e-visa; a medical is not currently required for issuance
Documents must be attested via HRD/Norka, MEA and the Saudi Embassy before applyingNot needed to apply; often needed after acceptance or on arrival
